Celestron StarSense Explorer LT 114AZ comes with an Alt-Az mount for beginner-friendly skywatching tracking. Jamie Carter Jamie Carter Jamie Carter Jamie Carter Jamie Carter Jamie Carter When we reviewed the Celestron StarSense Explorer LT 114AZ, which is the lightweight tripod-mounted version of this telescope, we thought that the tripod was flimsy and affected our ability to observe and navigate to night sky objects. This version of the telescope doesn't have a tripod and has a Dobsonian design, which is very sturdy when used on a stable surface like a table or bench.

It really shines during planetary observation such as the moon and Jupiter , but it did struggle with deep-sky objects. The supplied eyepieces are ideal for planetary viewing, but if you wanted to upgrade your setup, you can always buy a separate set of the best eyepieces .

Key features: 4.5-inch (114 mm) aperture, 450mm focal length (f/4), alt-azimuth tabletop Dobsonian base, StarSense Explorer smartphone app integration, 1.25-inch rack-and-pinion focuser, StarPointer red-dot finderscope.
